text:
If a thorn wounds me, I turn away from the thorn,

...but I do not abhor it! When envious meanness

drives the darts of its spite into me,

my foot silently dodges it, and makes its way

toward a purer atmosphere of love and charity.


Grudges? What use are they! What do grudges achieve?

They neither staunch wounds nor correct evil.

My rosebush has barely time to give flowers,

and does not squander sap on piercing spikes:

if my enemy passes near my rosebush,


he will carry away the roses of subtlest essence;

and if he notices in them some lively red,

it will be that of the blood which his malevolence

shed yesterday, when wounding me with rancor and violence,

and which the rosebush returns, changed into a flower of peace!

translation.title: If a Thorn Wounds Me, I Turn Away from the Thorn!
translation.editorial_note: The translation keeps the thorn-and-rose argument for transforming injury into peace.
